title: Serving Requests Before Essential Bootstrap Is Ready
pattern: A server admits ordinary application requests before required dependencies have completed initialization and essential configuration, files/assets, database connectivity, and schema prerequisites have been validated.
why_bad: Clients can reach a partially initialized application and receive crashes, hangs, or transaction failures caused by missing resources rather than legitimate request errors, creating a storm of failed transactions and cascading downstream alerts.
detection: Trace startup ordering from configuration parsing and dependency initialization/validation (DI, database pools, schema and asset checks) to listener activation, request acceptance, and dispatch. Flag paths that can execute application work requiring resources that are not yet available; an early socket bind alone is insufficient if a reliable readiness gate prevents unsafe dispatch.
fix: Finish initialization and validate the resources essential to the offered application operations before enabling their request processing. On bootstrap failure, do not advertise those operations as ready. If early binding/buffering is intentional, enforce the readiness gate through every dispatch path rather than relying solely on startup code order.
source: Michael Nygard, *Release It!*, Section 14.3 / passage [280, 587]; *Release It!*, page 266 [266, 686].
